title: Child checkup
what: The pediatrician checks how your child is growing and developing. Sometimes other doctors, tests, and vaccines are added to the visit.
why: On a schedule that depends on age, most often in the first year of life. Also before kindergarten, school, camp, and sports clubs.
duration: usually 20 to 30 minutes with the pediatrician. Longer with other doctors
tell_doctor: Any worries about health, sleep, eating, or behavior
Allergies and reactions to past vaccines
What medicines and vitamins you give
What illnesses your child has had recently

prepare.title: Feeling well
prepare.text: If your child is ill, let the clinic know. The checkup and vaccine are usually rescheduled.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: If urine or blood tests are needed, ask the clinic how to collect urine and whether your child needs to fast.

prepare.title: Mood
prepare.text: Calmly tell your child the doctor will see how they are growing. Do not scare them with shots.

bring: Your child's documents and vaccination record
Notes from past checkups and tests
A diaper, a blanket, a bottle, or a snack
steps: Your child is weighed and measured. For babies, the head size is measured too
The pediatrician asks about sleep, eating, and development
The doctor listens to the heart and lungs, looks at the throat and skin, and feels the belly
The doctor checks development for age: how your child holds their head, walks, and talks
The pediatrician may refer you to other doctors or for tests
If a vaccine is due, the doctor will discuss it with you
feel: The checkup itself does not hurt
A baby may cry when undressed. This is normal
If a vaccine is given, a quick prick
after: The doctor gives advice and tells you when the next checkup is
Write down questions that come up at home, for the next visit
After a vaccine, you are usually advised to wait at the clinic for about 30 minutes
red_flags: Trouble breathing, a swollen face, or a rash all over right after a vaccine
Seizures, floppiness, or your child is hard to wake
A high fever in a baby under 3 months: call emergency services

faq.q: How often should I take my child to the pediatrician if all is well?
faq.a: In the first year, usually every month, then less often, on your clinic's schedule. A separate checkup is needed before kindergarten and school.

faq.q: Can we go to a checkup if my child has a runny nose?
faq.a: Let the clinic know. The checkup can sometimes go ahead, but the vaccine is usually postponed until your child is well.

reminders.text: Child checkup tomorrow. Get the vaccination record, documents, and a favorite toy ready.
